# UnlearnBench

[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

[![CI](https://github.com/soumikbhatta/unlearnbench/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/soumikbhatta/unlearnbench/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**Multi-Attack Verification for Machine Unlearning**

> *CS 590NN/690NN — Neural Networks in AI and Neuroscience · University of Massachusetts Amherst · Spring 2026*

---

## Overview

Machine unlearning is the problem of removing the influence of specific training data from a model without full retraining — motivated by regulatory requirements such as GDPR's "right to be forgotten." Existing methods are typically verified using a single signal: **Membership Inference Attack (MIA)**, which tests whether an adversary can still identify whether a data point was in the training set.

**The problem:** MIA can be defeated through confidence calibration while structural traces of forgotten data remain in model weights, activations, and the loss landscape. A model can *look* unlearned without *being* unlearned.

**UnlearnBench** addresses this with an ensemble of five verification signals applied uniformly across multiple unlearning baselines and datasets, enabling a rigorous oracle-grounded comparison.

---

## Research Question

> Can multi-signal verification expose residual data traces that single-signal MIA verification misses?

We define the **Oracle Gap** as the measurable distance between an unlearned model and a model retrained from scratch (the gold standard). A perfect unlearning method has zero Oracle Gap across all verification signals.

---

## Verification Signals

| Signal                           | Description                                                   | Tier     |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| **MIA**                          | Membership inference attack on the forget set                 | Tier 1   |
| **Oracle Gap (Weight Distance)** | L2 / cosine distance to retrained oracle parameters           | Tier 1   |
| **Activation Analysis**          | Hidden-layer response similarity on forgotten vs. unseen data | Tier 2   |
| **Feature Attribution**          | Saliency map alignment on forgotten samples (GradCAM)         | Tier 2   |
| **Loss Landscape**               | Hessian eigenspectrum trace on the forget set                 | Tier 3 ↗ |

---

## Baseline Unlearning Methods

| Method                | Type                                                        | Reference                       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **Fisher Forgetting** | Approximate — noise injection via Fisher Information Matrix | Golatkar et al., NeurIPS 2020   |
| **Gradient Ascent**   | Approximate — maximize loss on forget set                   | —                               |
| **SISA Training**     | Exact — sharded training with selective retraining          | Bourtoule et al., IEEE S&P 2021 |

---

## Datasets

| Dataset         | Tasks                                             | Difficulty   |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| **Split-MNIST** | 5 binary classification tasks (digit pairs)       | Baseline     |
| **CIFAR-10**    | 5 tasks (2 classes each)                          | Medium       |
| **CelebA**      | Attribute-level forgetting (40 binary attributes) | Stretch goal |

---

## Repository Layout

```
unlearnbench/
├── src/unlearnbench/          # Core library
│   ├── datasets/              # Split-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CelebA loaders
│   ├── methods/               # Fisher, gradient ascent, SISA
│   ├── signals/               # MIA, oracle gap, activation, attribution, loss landscape
│   ├── models/                # Small CNN / MLP backbones
│   └── utils/                 # Seeding, metrics, logging
├── configs/                   # YAML experiment configs (per dataset)
├── experiments/               # Shell scripts for batch runs
├── results/                   # Output tables and figures (gitignored for large files)
├── tests/                     # Unit + integration tests
├── paper/                     # LaTeX proposal writeup and final report
├── docs/
│   ├── proposal/              # Submitted proposal deck
│   └── study_notes/           # Team technical reference docs
├── run_benchmark.py           # Unified benchmark entrypoint
├── pyproject.toml             # Build system + tool configuration
└── requirements.txt           # Pinned dependencies
```

---

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/soumikbhatta/unlearnbench.git
cd unlearnbench

python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Run the first benchmark: gradient ascent on Split-MNIST, verify with MIA + Oracle Gap
python run_benchmark.py \
  --dataset split_mnist \
  --method gradient_ascent \
  --signals mia oracle_gap \
  --seed 42
```

    68→## Core concepts (know these before writing code)
    69→
    70→### Oracle Gap
    71→The distance between an **unlearned model** and a model **retrained from scratch** on the retain set only.
    72→The retrained model is the gold standard — it never saw the forget set.
    73→```
    74→Oracle Gap = some_metric(unlearned_model, oracle_model)
    75→```
    76→Implemented metrics: L2 parameter distance, cosine similarity.

    79→### Forget set / Retain set
    80→The training data is split into:
    81→- **Forget set (F):** data points the model should "unlearn"
    82→- **Retain set (R):** everything else — model keeps this knowledge
    83→
    84→In Split-MNIST, each "task" is a pair of digit classes. Forget set = one full task (e.g. digits 0+1).

    94→- Add noise inversely proportional to Fisher importance

---

## What is this project?

**UnlearnBench** is a CS 590NN course project at UMass Amherst (Spring 2026).

The project builds a benchmark to evaluate machine unlearning methods.

**Machine unlearning:** removing the influence of specific training data from a model,
required by GDPR "right to be forgotten." The standard way to verify that unlearning
worked is a Membership Inference Attack (MIA). We argue MIA alone is insufficient —
a model can fool MIA while retaining structural traces of the "forgotten" data in its
weights, activations, and loss landscape.

**Our contribution:** run 3 unlearning baselines through 5 verification signals and compare
them against an oracle (model retrained from scratch). We call the gap between an unlearned
model and the oracle the **Oracle Gap**.

## Core concepts (know these before writing code)

### Oracle Gap
The distance between an **unlearned model** and a model **retrained from scratch** on the retain set only.
The retrained model is the gold standard — it never saw the forget set.
```
Oracle Gap = some_metric(unlearned_model, oracle_model)
```
Implemented metrics: L2 parameter distance, cosine similarity.
Perfect unlearning = Oracle Gap of 0 across all signals.

### Forget set / Retain set
The training data is split into:
- **Forget set (F):** data points the model should "unlearn"
- **Retain set (R):** everything else — model keeps this knowledge

In Split-MNIST, each "task" is a pair of digit classes. Forget set = one full task (e.g. digits 0+1).

### The 3 unlearning methods

**1. Gradient Ascent** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/gradient_ascent.py`)
- Maximize (instead of minimize) cross-entropy loss on the forget set
- Fast, simple. Risk: destabilizes retain performance if too aggressive

**2. Fisher Forgetting** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/fisher.py`)
- Measure which weights are important for the retain set (Fisher Information diagonal)
- Add noise inversely proportional to Fisher importance
- Based on: Golatkar et al. NeurIPS 2020

**3. SISA Training** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/sisa.py` — not yet implemented)
- Shard the training data. Train on each shard separately. To unlearn, only retrain the affected shard.
- Exact unlearning (provably correct). More expensive upfront.
- Based on: Bourtoule et al. IEEE S&P 2021

**Tier 1 (implement first):**
- `signals/mia.py` — Membership Inference Attack: can an adversary tell if a sample was in training? AUC ~0.5 = looks unlearned.
- `signals/oracle_gap.py` — L2/cosine distance between unlearned model and oracle model parameters.

**Tier 2 (implement after Tier 1 works):**
- `signals/activation_analysis.py` — do hidden layers still respond to forget-set data? (not yet started)
- `signals/feature_attribution.py` — GradCAM saliency on forget-set images (not yet started)

    p.add_argument("--results-dir", type=Path, default=Path("results"))
    p.add_argument("--checkpoint-dir", type=Path, default=Path("checkpoints"))
    return p.parse_args()


def resolve_device(device_str: str) -> str:
    if device_str == "auto":
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            return "cuda"
        if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
            return "mps"
        return "cpu"
    return device_str


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    set_seed(args.seed)

    device = resolve_device(args.device)
    logger.info("=" * 60)
    logger.info("UnlearnBench")
    logger.info("  dataset=%s  method=%s  signals=%s", args.dataset, args.method, args.signals)
    logger.info("  device=%s  seed=%d  epochs=%d", device, args.seed, args.epochs)
    logger.info("=" * 60)

    # ── 1. Data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    retain_loader, forget_loader, test_loader, oracle_loader = get_dataset(
        args.dataset, seed=args.seed, forget_task=args.forget_task, batch_size=args.batch_size
    )

    # ── 2. Base model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    in_channels = 1 if args.dataset == "split_mnist" else 3
    model = get_model("simple_cnn", in_channels=in_channels, num_classes=10)
    args.checkpoint_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ckpt_path = args.checkpoint_dir / f"base_{args.dataset}_seed{args.seed}.pt"

    if ckpt_path.exists():
        logger.info("Loading existing checkpoint: %s", ckpt_path)
        model.load_state_dict(torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location=device))
        model = model.to(device)
    else:
        logger.info("Training base model (%d epochs)...", args.epochs)
        model = train(
            model,
            retain_loader,
            test_loader,
            epochs=args.epochs,
            lr=args.lr,
            device=device,
            checkpoint_path=str(ckpt_path),
        )

    base_metrics = evaluate(model, test_loader, device)
    logger.info("Base model | test_acc=%.4f", base_metrics["accuracy"])

    # ── 3. Oracle model (retrained from scratch on retain only) ───────
    logger.info("Training oracle model (retain only, %d epochs)...", args.epochs)
    oracle = get_model("simple_cnn", in_channels=in_channels, num_classes=10)
    oracle = train(
        oracle, retain_loader, test_loader, epochs=args.epochs, lr=args.lr, device=device
    )

    # ── 4. Unlearning ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    logger.info("Applying unlearning method: %s", args.method)
    unlearner = get_method(args.method, device=device)
    unlearned = unlearner.unlearn(model, forget_loader, retain_loader)

    unlearned_metrics = evaluate(unlearned, test_loader, device)
    logger.info("Unlearned model | test_acc=%.4f", unlearned_metrics["accuracy"])

    # ── 5. Verification signals ───────────────────────────────────────
    signals = get_signals(args.signals, device=device)
    signal_results: dict[str, dict] = {}

    for signal in signals:
        logger.info("Running signal: %s", signal.name)
        if signal.name == "mia":
            result = signal.compute(unlearned, forget_loader, test_loader)
            signal_results["mia"] = {
                "attack_auc": result.attack_auc,
                "attack_accuracy": result.attack_accuracy,
            }
        elif signal.name == "oracle_gap":
            result = signal.compute(unlearned, oracle)
            signal_results["oracle_gap"] = {
                "l2_distance": result.l2_distance,
                "cosine_similarity": result.cosine_similarity,
            }

    # ── 6. Results ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    output = {
        "config": {
            "dataset": args.dataset,
            "method": args.method,
            "signals": args.signals,
            "forget_task": args.forget_task,
            "epochs": args.epochs,
            "seed": args.seed,
            "device": device,
        },
        "base_model": base_metrics,
        "unlearned_model": unlearned_metrics,
        "signals": signal_results,
    }

    args.results_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = args.results_dir / f"{args.dataset}_{args.method}_seed{args.seed}.json"
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(output, f, indent=2)

    logger.info("Results saved → %s", out_path)
    logger.info("=" * 60)
    logger.info("DONE")
    mia_auc = signal_results.get("mia", {}).get("attack_auc", float("nan"))
    oracle_l2 = signal_results.get("oracle_gap", {}).get("l2_distance", float("nan"))
    logger.info("  MIA AUC:         %.4f  (ideal: 0.50)", mia_auc)
    logger.info("  Oracle Gap (L2): %.6f (ideal: 0.00)", oracle_l2)
    logger.info("=" * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

---

## 1. What is machine unlearning?

**The problem:** Once a model is trained, it encodes information about every training data point in its weights. If a user requests data deletion (GDPR "right to be forgotten"), simply deleting the raw data is not enough — the model's weights still contain traces.

**The goal:** Remove the influence of a specific "forget set" F from a trained model M, producing an unlearned model M' that behaves as if F was never in the training data.

**The gold standard (Oracle):** Train a fresh model from scratch on only the retain set R (everything except F). This retrained model is the oracle — perfect unlearning equals the oracle.

**Why not always retrain?** Retraining from scratch is expensive. For large models, it can take days/weeks. Approximate unlearning methods aim to achieve oracle-level forgetting in minutes.

### Exact vs. Approximate Unlearning

| Type            | Description                                              | Example                            |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| **Exact**       | Provably produces same distribution as oracle retraining | SISA                               |
| **Approximate** | Heuristic, faster, but may leave traces                  | Fisher Forgetting, Gradient Ascent |

---

## 2. Our three baseline methods

### Gradient Ascent
- **Idea:** Instead of minimizing loss on F, maximize it. This degrades the model's accuracy on the forget set.
- **Code:** `src/unlearnbench/methods/gradient_ascent.py`
- **Risk:** Too many steps → destabilizes retain set performance. Tune `steps` carefully.
- **Expected behavior:** MIA AUC drops, but Oracle Gap (L2) may remain high.

### Fisher Forgetting (Golatkar et al. 2020)
- **Idea:** Parameters important for the retain set (high Fisher Information) get low noise. Parameters important only for the forget set get high noise.
- **Code:** `src/unlearnbench/methods/fisher.py`
- **Key parameter:** `noise_scale` (α) — higher = more forgetting but more retain damage.
- **Expected behavior:** Should pass MIA, but Oracle Gap signals may reveal residual traces.

### SISA Training (Bourtoule et al. 2021)
- **Idea:** During training, shard the data into K slices. To unlearn a sample, only retrain the shard containing it. Provably exact.
- **Code:** `src/unlearnbench/methods/sisa.py` — **NOT YET IMPLEMENTED** (Phase 3 target)
- **Tradeoff:** Requires training K shards. More expensive upfront, but unlearning is cheap.

---

## 3. What are we trying to prove?

**Core claim:** MIA alone is an insufficient verification signal for machine unlearning.

A model can be "MIA-clean" (an attacker cannot infer the forget set from outputs) while still retaining structural traces in:
- Parameter weights (measurable via Oracle Gap)
- Internal activations (measurable via Activation Analysis)
- Loss landscape curvature (measurable via Hessian analysis)

**Our hypothesis:** Fisher Forgetting and Gradient Ascent will pass MIA verification but fail on Oracle Gap and/or activation signals. SISA, as an exact method, should achieve near-zero Oracle Gap.

---

## 4. Benchmark output format

Every experiment produces a JSON file under `results/`. Format:

```json
{
  "config": {
    "dataset": "split_mnist",
    "method": "gradient_ascent",
    "signals": ["mia", "oracle_gap"],
    "forget_task": 0,
    "epochs": 10,
    "seed": 42
  },
  "base_model": {"accuracy": 0.97, "loss": 0.12},
  "unlearned_model": {"accuracy": 0.94, "loss": 0.18},
  "signals": {
    "mia": {"attack_auc": 0.53, "attack_accuracy": 0.52},
    "oracle_gap": {"l2_distance": 0.024, "cosine_similarity": 0.999}
  }
}
```

**Interpretation guide:**
- `mia.attack_auc` → ideal: 0.50 (random). Higher = attacker can still identify forget set.
- `oracle_gap.l2_distance` → ideal: 0.00. Higher = unlearned model differs more from oracle.
- `oracle_gap.cosine_similarity` → ideal: 1.00. Lower = parameter directions differ from oracle.

Here is a comprehensive overview of this repository:

---

## UnlearnBench — What This Repo Is About

### Core Problem

**Machine unlearning** is the task of removing the influence of specific training data from a trained model, without retraining from scratch. This is required by laws like GDPR's "right to be forgotten."

The standard way to verify unlearning succeeded is a **Membership Inference Attack (MIA)** — test whether an adversary can still detect if a data point was in the training set.

**The flaw this project exposes:** A model can be manipulated to *look* unlearned under MIA (e.g., via confidence calibration) while still retaining structural traces of the "forgotten" data in its weights, activations, and loss landscape.

---

### What This Repo Builds

**UnlearnBench** is a benchmark that evaluates unlearning methods using **5 verification signals** simultaneously instead of just MIA:

| Signal | What it measures |
|---|---|
| MIA | Can an attacker identify if data was in training? |
| Oracle Gap (Weight Distance) | How far are the weights from a model retrained from scratch? |
| Activation Analysis | Do hidden layers still respond to forgotten data? |
| Feature Attribution (GradCAM) | Does the model still "look at" features from the forgotten data? |
| Loss Landscape (Hessian) | Are there second-order traces in the loss surface? |

The key concept is the **Oracle Gap** — the measurable distance between an unlearned model and a model retrained from scratch (the gold standard). Perfect unlearning = Oracle Gap of zero.

---

### Three Unlearning Methods Being Benchmarked

| Method | Type | Idea |
|---|---|---|
| **Gradient Ascent** | Approximate | Maximize (instead of minimize) loss on the forget set |
| **Fisher Forgetting** (Golatkar 2020) | Approximate | Inject noise into weights, scaled by Fisher Information |
| **SISA Training** (Bourtoule 2021) | Exact/Provable | Shard training data; only retrain the shard containing forgotten data |

---

### Datasets

- **Split-MNIST** — 5 binary classification tasks (digit pairs), used as baseline
- **CIFAR-10** — 5 tasks (2 classes each), medium difficulty
- **CelebA** — attribute-level forgetting (stretch goal)

---

### Current State

The repo is a **course project (CS 590NN, UMass Amherst, Spring 2026)** in early implementation phase:
- Scaffolds exist for dataset loaders, the CNN model, and the two Tier-1 signals (MIA, Oracle Gap)
- The main pipeline (`run_benchmark.py`) is wired up end-to-end
- Tier-2 signals (activation analysis, feature attribution) and SISA are not yet implemented
- Your role (Sagnik) is: `src/unlearnbench/datasets/` and `src/unlearnbench/utils/metrics.py`

---

### The Central Research Question

> **Can multi-signal verification expose residual data traces that single-signal MIA verification misses?**

The hypothesis is that approximate methods (Fisher Forgetting, Gradient Ascent) will pass MIA but fail on Oracle Gap and activation signals, while SISA (exact) will achieve near-zero Oracle Gap.
